chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Uyaynah the seller of reeds, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I enter the mosque on a day of intense heat, and I dislike praying on the pebbles, so I spread my garment and prostrate upon it.' He said, 'Yes, there is no harm in that.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to spread a cloth to prostrate on during prayer if the ground is uncomfortable?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of using a garment as a prayer mat (*mubah*) to avoid discomfort from pebbles or heat, reflecting the Shia principle of removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in worship. It underscores that the primary requirement for prostration is a clean, natural surface, allowing for practical adaptations to maintain concentration (*khushu*) during prayer.
